findings.claim: The new README section and MsgPack004 doc state that diagnostics for members of referenced-assembly types are deliberately reported by the defining assembly rather than the consumer. This matches the recorded convention that types from referenced assemblies are not analysed. The suppression of MemberNeedsKey and the other location-less diagnostics for metadata types is therefore deliberate and not a defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no diagnostics from the compiling assembly; the defining assembly validates its own types. Dropping MsgPack004 for metadata closed generic structs is consistent with this.

findings.claim: The new ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter wraps every diagnostic reported through reportDiagnostic. Any diagnostic with Location.None, or whose syntax tree is outside the compilation, is now silently dropped. This could hide legitimate diagnostics whose location is currently null, for example GetIdentifierLocation returning null for types in partial or generated code. Given recent false-positive and false-negative churn in analyzer diagnostics, this behavior change is broader than the crash fix needs.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the existing reportDiagnostic call sites that pass a possibly-null Location (e.g. GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation results). Check whether any previously reported with Location.None and now get dropped. Run the existing analyzer test suite (MsgPack003-018) to detect regressions.
